History of Evolutionary Thought
¨Prior to Darwin
¤The view of nature was determined by deep-seated beliefs held to be intractable truths rather than experimentation and observation
¤Biologists had slowly begun to accept various new ideas of evolution –species change over time
¨Evolution is the Unifying Principle of Biology
¤Explains the unity and diversity of life
nSimilarities between living things reflect recent common ancestors
nDissimilarities between living things reflect ancient common ancestor
explanation: Before Charles Darwin, the prevailing view of the natural world was dictated by deep-seated traditional beliefs accepted as absolute truths, rather than scientific observation and active experimentation. However, biologists gradually began to entertain the idea that species change over time, laying the groundwork for evolutionary theory. Today, evolution is considered the unifying principle of biology because it explains both the unity and diversity of life. The similarities observed among living things point to recent common ancestry, while the dissimilarities point to more ancient common ancestry.

opts: Similarities reflect ancient common ancestors, whereas dissimilarities reflect recent common ancestors.
